# Phantom module map

Snapshot of the source tree at `00b72c2ea60de124051bb687a80f94663378d3b5` on 2026-11-13, with file-level dependencies, test references, history and host-script evidence.

## Standard header

- Read-only analysis + one docs file. No runtime edits, no `~/.ashlr-runs` modifications.
- `npx vitest run` not needed (docs-only); run `npm run check:docs` before any later PR.
- No secret values. Any later landing uses `publish.sh` (fork-only). No `--admin`, no force-push. No em dashes.
- Article 2: use `--json` where CLI surfaces are touched; no CLI surfaces changed. The generated `docs/llms.txt` entry indexes this document.
- Delivery includes this report, its generated documentation-index entry and root `BRIDGE_NOTES.md`. The final job instruction requires uncommitted changes: no commit, push, tag, publication or PR was performed.

## Reading the inventory

The inventory covers every Git-tracked file in the eleven requested roots, including tests, styles, assets, configuration and operational templates. It does not silently drop non-TypeScript files. Each file appears once under its full repository directory; the Path cell is relative to that directory. Concatenate the directory heading and cell to recover the full path. Directory summaries include files directly in that directory, not recursive totals.

The source inventory is complete. The installed operational-bin inventory is incomplete because macOS returned `Operation not permitted` when listing `~/.ashlr-runs/bin`. Runtime presence, loaded services, digest pins, drift and live/legacy/dead status remain unknown. The operational section inventories manifest and launch-reference evidence without claiming access to the directory.

### Measurement rules

- Import graph: TypeScript compiler API AST parsing of all 10827 tracked TS/JS files across the repository, including tests and scripts. Count static imports, re-exports, type-only imports, `import()` with literal arguments, `require()`, import types and Vite literal `import.meta.glob` patterns. Resolve local `.js` specifiers to source `.ts`/`.tsx`, directories to index modules, and known `dist/` build paths to `src/`. Parse Python import statements separately; resolve CSS/HTML local asset references.
- Dep is the number of distinct direct non-test dependent files in that graph, including type-only consumers, re-exporting barrels, glob loaders and local asset consumers. Tests are excluded from Dep. It measures files, not symbol uses, runtime traffic or external package consumers.
- Test IDs resolve to exact paths in the test dictionary. They identify direct imports or literal source-path references by tests, including source-inspection tests. They are static coverage evidence, not executed line/branch coverage. Transitive integration coverage and computed test paths may be missed. SELF means the row is itself test/fixture support; it is not a claim that a separate test covers it. none found means no direct static mapping was found.
- Ref counts distinct non-test literal code/configuration references beyond importers. This catches `new URL` child workers, computed-extension skill-audit workers, shell helpers and manifest registrations. Package exports, Raycast command registration and ambient declarations are ENTRY exemptions. Historical evidence JSON and CI affected-file inventories are excluded as liveness evidence.
- LOC is physical text lines, including comments and blanks. Binary assets use n/a. It is an approximate maintenance-size metric, not executable LOC. GOD marks every file over 2,000 text lines, including styles and tests.
- Date is the last observed reachable file-changing Git commit date, using committer calendar dates at the pinned HEAD and no rename following. A complete separate bare history was fetched into `/tmp` after the eleven-commit worktree history proved insufficient. A combined path-limited `git log --name-only` supplied dates, with per-file `git log -1` fallback for absent paths. Date-only comparisons and merge/path simplification can affect age; dates are not deployment times. Directory Date is the maximum file date.
- CORE is conservative: a committed Tier-1 root/closure member, public SDK entrypoint, a module with at least ten direct dependents, or an explicit primary CLI/browser/dispatcher/publisher/restocker/sync entry. It is an architectural review label, not new execution authority.
- FEATURE is other product code. PERIPHERY covers tests/fixtures, assets/configuration/docs, ambient declarations, Raycast/TUI/planning tools and host support that do not meet CORE criteria. DEAD-CANDIDATE requires zero importers, zero mapped tests, zero observed operational references, no known entrypoint, and at least 90 days since its last change. All conditions are necessary; no module satisfies them at this snapshot.
- Flags: T1-root/T1-closure use the committed `test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json`, not a regenerated authority snapshot; ENTRY is a non-import entrypoint; AMBIENT is a declaration; STALE is 90 days without a change; ORPHAN is no importers/tests/known entrypoint or operational refs; REF-ONLY is the same with operational refs; TEST-ONLY means no observed non-test importer/reference or entrypoint despite mapped tests. These last three are investigation signals, not deletion authority. D: identifiers refer to the overlap table.

Purposes are concise descriptions derived from module headers, exported symbols and directory roles; the major entrypoints and shortlists were reviewed individually. Dynamic dispatch, Python importlib, arbitrary shell sourcing, runtime-created paths, external SDK users and operating-system registrations can escape static analysis.

### Reproduction

No analysis dependency was added to the repository. The analyzer used the already installed `typescript` package; `ts-morph` and `madge` were absent. Scratch scripts and raw JSON live outside the worktree in `/tmp`. To refresh this snapshot, enumerate the same tracked roots, parse the import forms above with `ts.createSourceFile`/`ts.forEachChild`, expand literal globs, build unique reverse-edge sets, join direct test/literal-reference sets, and apply the stated classification rules. Use a complete history and preserve entrypoint exemptions.

```sh
git ls-files src/cli src/core src/web-ui src/mcp src/tui src/fleet src/api src/raycast src/planning contrib/mac fleet
git log --format="COMMIT %cs %H" --name-only --no-renames HEAD -- src/cli src/core src/web-ui src/mcp src/tui src/fleet src/api src/raycast src/planning contrib/mac fleet
git log -1 --format="%cs %H" HEAD -- <module-path>
node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs
node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs --check
npm run check:docs
node scripts/verify-changed.mjs
```

## Overlapping functionality

These are consolidation leads based on responsibilities and contracts. They are not assertions that one implementation can replace another. Token-normalized whole-module comparison of production TS/JS files of at least 30 lines and 100 tokens found no exact duplicate group; this does not rule out copied functions or near-duplicates.

### Q1: Queue state and claims

`src/core/queue/store.ts`, `src/core/queue/schema.ts`, `src/core/drive/queue-v1.ts`, `src/core/drive/nodes/queue-v1.ts`, `src/core/drive/nodes/router.ts`, `src/core/fleet/shared-store.ts`, `src/core/verse/feedback-queue.ts`, `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`, `contrib/mac/queue_gate.py`.

JSON queue snapshots, node leases, shared-store tasks and filesystem dispatcher markers have distinct state machines. Consolidate adapters and contract vocabulary before considering a single storage authority.

### Q2: Admission and restock

`src/core/queue/admission.ts`, `src/core/queue/lint.ts`, `src/core/drive/router-lint.ts`, `src/core/drive/queuegen.ts`, `src/core/drive/restock-plan.ts`, `contrib/mac/restock.py`, `contrib/mac/self-supply.py`, `contrib/mac/fleet_controller.py`.

Multiple admission, lint and replenishment paths can disagree about READY, pool, tier and dependency gates. Compare shared fixtures; never bypass a pin to unify them.

### R1: Routing and selection

`src/core/fleet/router.ts`, `src/core/routing/router.ts`, `src/core/routing/selector.ts`, `src/core/routing/scheduling.ts`, `src/core/drive/pool-routing.ts`, `src/core/drive/nodes/router.ts`, `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`.

Legacy WorkItem backend/model selection, account-seat ranking, node routing and pool admission solve overlapping allocation problems at different boundaries.

### R2: Capacity and usage

`src/core/fabric/resource-monitor.ts`, `src/core/resources/pacing.ts`, `src/core/routing/headroom.ts`, `src/core/routing/budget-store.ts`, `src/core/daemon/capacity-publisher.ts`, `src/core/routing/capacity-history.ts`.

Measured quota, budget metadata, subscription publication and routing headroom are split across fabric/resources/routing. Preserve provenance and unknown values when sharing readers.

### C1: Owner messages and outbound requests

`src/core/comms/dispatch.ts`, `src/core/comms/owner-thread.ts`, `src/core/comms/owner-live-transport.ts`, `src/core/comms/email-outbox.ts`, `src/core/cos/drafts.ts`, `src/core/cos/intake.ts`, `src/core/fleet/channel-envelope.ts`, `src/core/agents/channel-policy.ts`.

Dispatch-cycle requests, canonical owner thread, email outbox, drafts and chief-of-staff intake each have delivery/idempotency state. A draft approval is not send authority.

### C2: Bus and task coordination

`src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.ts`, `src/core/agents/adapters/bus.ts`, `src/core/fleet/bus-envelope.ts`, `src/core/fleet/bus-inbox.ts`, `src/core/fleet/channel-bus-publish.ts`, `src/core/fleet/shared-store.ts`.

Agent Bus v2, channel envelopes and the SharedStore task queue overlap in identity, expiry and claim semantics. Keep coordination distinct from execution authorization.

### W1: Interactive and autonomous runs

`src/core/run/orchestrator.ts`, `src/core/verse/session-engine.ts`, `src/core/fleet/manager.ts`, `src/core/daemon/loop.ts`.

Interactive sessions, task runs, fleet attempts and resident ticks each orchestrate work. Share cancellation and result contracts only after comparing their authority boundaries.

### O1: Host lifecycle and session observation

`src/core/drive/supervisor.ts`, `src/core/daemon/loop.ts`, `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`, `contrib/mac/fleet_controller.py`, `contrib/mac/host_session_tick.py`, `contrib/mac/host_session_runtime.py`, `contrib/mac/process_snapshot.py`.

Several supervisors and host observation layers coexist. Repository source does not prove installed runtime adoption; distinguish observation helpers from launch owners.

### O2: Publication and merge

`src/core/inbox/merge.ts`, `src/core/integrations/github.ts`, `contrib/mac/publish.sh`, `contrib/mac/integrated-merge.py`, `contrib/mac/pr-create.sh`.

SDK merge paths and the pinned host publisher overlap in verification, fork publication and merge handling. Keep the sanctioned publisher and security gates authoritative.

### U1: Console generations

`src/core/web/server.ts`, `src/core/web/public/app.js`, `src/core/web/public/styles.css`, `src/web-ui/main.tsx`, `src/web-ui/app/App.tsx`, `src/web-ui/routes/verse/VerseApp.tsx`.

The legacy static dashboard and React console coexist. Trace HTTP asset mounts and supported URLs before treating the static assets as obsolete.

### F1: Fleet namespaces

`src/fleet/risk.ts`, `src/fleet/replay.ts`, `src/core/fleet/status.ts`, `src/core/fleet/router.ts`, `src/cli/fleet.ts`, `src/mcp/fleet.ts`.

Top-level src/fleet hosts risk/replay helpers; src/core/fleet owns a much larger runtime and projections. Similar names do not establish duplicate implementations.

- `src/api/plugin.ts` has no local production importers but is the published `./plugin` export in `package.json`.
- `src/cli/skills-audit-process.ts` is a worker selected through a computed extension by `src/cli/skills.ts`.

- `*.pane.ts`/`*.pane.tsx`, unit `register.ts` modules and section components are loaded with Vite glob discovery.
- Grokbot, engineering, fleet-history and read-projection workers are launched through URL/process paths. Zero static imports do not establish that these workers are unused.

## Operational scripts: report only

Access to `~/.ashlr-runs/bin/*` is unavailable. The directory listing was refused, and execution of the read-only `launchctl list` probe was also refused. Therefore no complete wildcard inventory, live digest comparison or dead-script finding is possible. Two unrelated plists were unparseable and excluded; their contents are not included. Only launchd Program/ProgramArguments were read, with script basenames retained; no environment-variable values were retained.

The following 84 names are the union of manifest rows, readable launchd bin-path references and literal references in the repository operational tree, including tests, documentation, candidate mirrors, the dispatcher, launcher candidate and publisher. These textual references alone do not establish runtime use. Source absence means no mirror was found at the declared/conventional path, not that the runtime file is missing. Manifests, templates and source mirrors are not evidence of a currently installed or running version.

Classification is reported on two axes: declared protection (pinned/managed/manual/unlisted), and observed lifecycle evidence. `live-candidate` means referenced by a readable installed plist, not proved running; `referenced` means manifest or source evidence only. `legacy` and `dead` are withheld for every name because runtime absence and reference completeness cannot be established. Pinned names retain their protection regardless of lifecycle uncertainty.

No file, service, TCC grant, pin, runtime permission or auth setting was changed.
